issues.description: Translation uses "Cloud" to refer to 云隐村, but glossary specifies "Kumogakure".

note: 修复后未复查；上面列的是修复前发现的问题

issues.quote: Hiruzen, you still haven't said how we're going to use them..." Danzo Shimura asked impatiently.
issues.description: The dialogue punctuation is off: the closing quotation mark precedes the attribution without a comma, making the sentence awkward. It should be punctuated with a comma before the closing quote and the dialogue tag outside. Suggested: "Hiruzen, you still haven't said how we're going to use them," Danzo Shimura asked impatiently.

issues.quote: He pulled out the necklace from his chest.
issues.description: Literal phrasing suggests pulling a necklace from inside his chest. Idiomatically, it should be "from his shirt" or "from inside his robes." Suggested: "He pulled the necklace out from under his shirt."

issues.quote: Hizashi naturally picked one up.
issues.description: This sentence introduces Hizashi abruptly without prior context in the scene, creating a referential gap that reads like a dangling subject. Clarify who Hizashi is or add a brief identifier. Suggested: "Hizashi Hyuga naturally picked one up" or "Hizashi, who stood nearby, naturally picked one up."

issues.quote: It was like listening to a storyteller, but the narrator had taken a sip of tea and deliberately refused to continue the next part... Such a tease!
issues.description: The imagery and phrasing feel calqued and awkward ("the narrator had taken a sip of tea and deliberately refused to continue the next part"). A more idiomatic rendering would streamline the metaphor. Suggested: "It was like listening to a storyteller who paused to sip tea and refused to continue... Such a tease!"

issues.quote: Even if he had made mistakes.
issues.description: This fragment stands alone without a main clause, reading like an incomplete thought. Combine it with the previous sentence or complete it. Suggested: "Even if he had made mistakes, ..." or attach it to the following sentence for coherence.

This appears to be untranslated internet slang/emoji-like text and is unclear to English readers. Either localize or clarify. Suggested: replace with an equivalent like "orz!!!" if intentional, or provide a clear phrase like "Please vote!"

issues.quote: Don't ride on their coattails!
issues.description: As a standalone interjection, this reads abrupt and idiomatically mismatched to the prior sentence. Clarify the subject or integrate it. Suggested: "Don't try to ride on their coattails," or fold it into the sentence: "They shouldn't try to ride on the Uchiha's coattails."

issues.quote: He could loosely interpret them as the 'Mist version' of the Uchiha, only even less popular.
issues.description: "Only even less popular" is clunky. A more idiomatic phrasing would be: "—a Mist version of the Uchiha, only even less well-regarded." or "...a Mist-side counterpart to the Uchiha, but even less popular."

issues.quote: The entanglements were too deep to explain in just a few words.
issues.description: "Entanglements" sounds literal and awkward here. A more idiomatic expression would be: "The ties were too complicated to explain briefly." or "The complications ran too deep to summarize in a few words."

issues.quote: Go argue that with the Empress Dowager herself!
issues.description: "Empress Dowager" feels like a borrowed cultural term and reads odd without context. If meant metaphorically, clarify or choose a more fitting title. Suggested: "Go argue that with the matriarch herself!" or "…with Lady Mito herself!"

issues.quote: Kakashi, with a strangely serene look in his eyes, was earnestly reading the sword technique notes his father had given him.
issues.description: While grammatical, "the sword technique notes" is awkwardly literal. For idiomatic clarity, add an article or rephrase: "the notes on sword techniques his father had given him" or "his father's swordsmanship notes."

issues.quote: Happy New Year's Day, second chapter! There will be another chapter around noon, maybe a little later.
issues.description: Reads like a direct author aside with literal phrasing. If kept as an author note, make it idiomatic: "Happy New Year—here's the second chapter! Another will be out around noon, maybe a bit later."

issues.quote: You're afraid that after you graduate, you'll have no rival in me and get lonely...
issues.description: The phrase "have no rival in me" is unidiomatic here. It reads awkwardly and blurs the intended meaning. A natural fix: "You'll be afraid that after you graduate, you won't have a rival like me and you'll get lonely," or "you won't have me as a rival and you'll get lonely."

issues.quote: Who could resist a companion who blushes while praising how awesome you are when sneaking a peek at you fishing?
issues.description: Pronoun reference and clause order are tangled. It reads as if "you" is the one sneaking a peek. Clearer: "Who could resist a companion who blushes while praising how awesome you are as he sneaks peeks at you fishing?"

issues.quote: Some people are just naturally drawn to each other.
issues.description: While grammatical, in this context following the prior sentence, it feels like a generic proverb inserted as a literal bridge, giving a translated, didactic tone. A more idiomatic segue: "Some people just click," or "Some people just hit it off."

issues.quote: a hot-blooded dead last
issues.description: "Dead last" is fine, but “hot-blooded dead last” sounds like a calque. More natural would be "a hotheaded underachiever" or "a hotheaded loser (at the bottom of the class)."

issues.quote: He often called out Obito, who was sneaking peeks from hiding, and invited him to eat together.
issues.description: “sneaking peeks from hiding” is stiff and literal. Also, "invited him to eat together" is awkward. More natural: "He often called Obito out when he caught him spying and invited him to grab a bite together," or "...and invited him to eat with him."

issues.quote: Kakashi put down the sword technique notes in his hand, his calm gaze shifting to a hint of melancholy, and spoke in a tone that sounded like a little adult:
issues.description: "like a little adult" is odd, and the sentence structure is clunky. Also, "the sword technique notes in his hand" is awkward. Suggested: "Kakashi set down his swordsmanship notes, his calm gaze shading into melancholy, and spoke in a tone that sounded far too adult."

issues.quote: Although the academy hadn't yet implemented an elite advanced class, objectively speaking, a clique had already formed.
issues.description: "elite advanced class" is redundant and awkward, and "objectively speaking" is stiff filler. Consider: "Although the academy hadn't implemented an advanced elite class yet, cliques had already formed." Also ensure plural agreement if multiple cliques are implied.

issues.quote: That Guy guy seemed to really admire that blond...
issues.description: Repetition and article use are awkward. If playing on the name "Guy," better: "That Guy seemed to really admire that blond(e)..." or "Guy really seemed to admire that blond(e) guy..."

issues.quote: lacking a sense of boundaries.
issues.description: This phrase feels clinical and translated in this casual narrative. More idiomatic: "with zero sense of boundaries" or "without any sense of boundaries," or even "no concept of boundaries."

issues.quote: So even before graduation, the bond between the three of them was as tight as a fully formed three-man squad.
issues.description: "fully formed three-man squad" sounds like a literal import from another language/anime term. A smoother phrasing: "as tight as an actual three-man team" or "as tight as a real squad."

issues.quote: Eh?
issues.description: As a standalone interjection, "Eh?" reads as a direct carryover from another language and can feel unnatural in English narrative here. More idiomatic: "Huh?" or "What?"

issues.quote: Even though I hate to admit it, you're definitely someone worth surpassing.
issues.description: Literal and stilted; native phrasing would be: "Even though I hate to admit it, you're definitely someone worth beating," or "worth aiming to surpass."

issues.quote: "Most? I don't know if that guy counts as an ordinary chunin..."
issues.description: "Most?" as a standalone echo of "Most chunin" is unclear. Better: "Most? I don't know if that guy even counts as an ordinary chunin..." or "Most? I’m not sure that guy counts as a typical chunin..."

issues.quote: his full-force sneak attack didn't even touch a hair on his head
issues.description: Calque-like phrasing. More idiomatic: "his all-out sneak attack didn't even graze him" or "didn't so much as ruffle a hair."

issues.quote: His youth burns like a little sun!
issues.description: Literal transcreation that reads odd in English. A more natural line that keeps the flavor: "His youthful spirit burns like a little sun!" or "His youth burns like the sun!"
